facts.raw_span: A 5‐year‐9‐month‐old, 170‐kg domestic llama mare
1‐week history of dyspnea and inspiratory noise
esophageal obstruction had been suspected by the referring veterinarian
spasmolytics and passage of a gastric tube did not improve the signs
bright, alert, in good condition (body‐condition score 3.5/5) with normal vital signs
10 × 8 × 3‐cm subcutaneous mass that was partially firm and fluctuant, slightly painful, and mildly warm
mild leukocytosis (23,690/µL; reference 8,700–17,500/µL)
neutrophilia (92.4%; reference 42.4–76.4%)
lymphopenia (3.0%; reference 7.0–32.5%)
no abnormalities on flexible endoscopy of the esophagus and trachea
well‐demarcated, heterogeneously echogenic, encapsulated mass with no communication with the trachea or esophagus and no intrinsic vascular flow on cervical ultrasonography
ventral soft‐tissue‐density mass in the mid‐to‐caudal cervical region causing a mild mass effect on the trachea on thoracic and cervical radiographs

concepts.why: The presence of a subcutaneous mass with signs of infection and inflammation earned this slot.
The ventral soft-tissue-density mass in the mid-to-caudal cervical region causing a mild mass effect on the trachea on thoracic and cervical radiographs is consistent with a soft tissue sarcoma.

The well-demarcated, heterogeneously echogenic, encapsulated mass with no communication with the trachea or esophagus and no intrinsic vascular flow, combined with the lack of abnormalities on flexible endoscopy of the esophagus and trachea, could be explained by a thyroglossal duct cyst.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a subcutaneous mass that was partially firm and fluctuant, slightly painful, and mildly warm, along with mild leukocytosis and neutrophilia, most strongly supports the diagnosis of Streptococcal abscess.
